 Most recent Most popular Confident-sounding Emegha speaks in Chelsea's programme published at 14:38 GMT 14:38 GMT 
 Chelsea v Leeds (15:00 GMT) 
 Nizaar Kinsella 
BBC Sport football reporter at Stamford Bridge 
 In Chelsea's matchday programme, striker Emmanuel Emegha has spoken about his determination to succeed after making his first start for the club.
 He said: "I'm a winner, I'm a fighter. I would do anything to win. If I need to block a ball with the front of my face, I will do it. I'm quick, I know how to make runs from behind, and I know that I can be a nightmare for all the defenders."
 Emegha added: "But nobody has seen me yet. I know everybody was like, 'Where is he?' or things like this, but it will come.
 "And I know that, when my time comes, I will be ready, and I know that the stadium will love my energy."
 Asked whether he could raise his game to Chelsea's level after joining from sister club Strasbourg, he said: "Yeah, that's why I know that at Chelsea I can and I will also do it.
 "Every player is different. There are some players, you buy them and straight away they are... boom! Me, I always need some time to adapt, and I've had a lot of injuries."

 Emegha gets his chance at Chelsea published at 14:34 GMT 14:34 GMT 
 Chelsea v Leeds (15:00 GMT) 
 Nizaar Kinsella 
BBC Sport football reporter at Stamford Bridge 
 Chelsea striker Emmanuel Emegha is making his first Chelsea start in any competition.
 It is the latest attempt by manager Xabi Alonso to replace Joao Pedro, having previously used Danny Welbeck, Morgan Rogers and Pedro Neto up front in his absence.
 In those matches, Chelsea have beaten only Manchester United and failed to score in three games.
 Emegha will be keen to prove he is the answer after being given his first real opportunity since joining sister club Strasbourg in the summer.

 Leaky Villa defence published at 14:32 GMT 14:32 GMT 
 Aston Villa v Sunderland (17:30 GMT) 
 Four goals conceded in 11 games is not what Aston Villa boss Unai Emery will want to see, but that is the reality he faces. 
 Emery addressed the stat yesterday: "We made a lot of errors conceding goals. We must defend better, with and without the ball - trying to lose less balls than we sometimes do. We are trying to show the players how important it is to get our style through possession, our shape on the field."

Football reporter at Etihad Stadium 
 Loud boos at full-time here, the home fans are not happy with what they have seen from their side.
 Manchester City's winless Premier League run extends to four games, but give Fulham credit, they were excellent.

 Well, plenty of talking points. 
 Manchester City's winless run continues, and they're now five points off leaders Arsenal having played a game more.
 But there was big VAR controversy with Erling Haaland's first-half equaliser ruled out.
 Fulham, meanwhile, are now a full three points clear of the drop zone and are on a bit of run.
